{{color|#0c0|high}} · [[List of administrative divisions of Vietnam by Human Development Index |1st]] }} The '''Red River Delta''' or '''Hong River Delta''' ({{langx|vi|Đồng bằng sông Hồng}}) is the flat low-lying plain formed by the [[Red River (Asia)|Red River]] and its distributaries merging with the [[Thái Bình River]] in [[Northern Vietnam]]. ''Hồng'' (紅) is a [[Sino-Vietnamese vocabulary|Sino-Vietnamese]] word for "red" or "crimson". The delta has the smallest area but highest population and population density of all [[Regions of Vietnam|regions in Vietnam]]. The region, measuring some {{convert|15,000|sqkm|sqmi|-3}} is well protected by a network of [[levee|dikes]]. It is an agriculturally rich and densely populated area. Most of the land is devoted to rice cultivation.Whitfield, D. ''Historical and Cultural Dictionary of Vietnam''. Metuchen, New Jersey: The Scarecrow Press, 1976. The Red River Delta, after [[2025 Vietnamese administrative reform|the 2025 merger of Vietnamese provinces and cities]], includes four [[provinces of Vietnam|provinces]], together with two municipalities (the capital [[Hanoi]], and the port of [[Haiphong]]).{{Cite web|url=https://nld.com.vn/dong-bang-song-hong-con-6-dia-phuong-thu-tuong-yeu-cau-phat-huy-vai-tro-dau-tau-196250920100419988.htm|title=Đồng bằng sông Hồng còn 6 địa phương, Thủ tướng yêu cầu phát huy vai trò đầu tàu|work=Nguoi Lao Dong|date=September 20, 2025|access-date=January 15, 2026}} It had a population of almost 23 million in 2019. In 2021, [[Paul Sidwell]] proposed that the locus of Proto-[[Austroasiatic languages|Austroasiatic]] languages was in this area about 4,000–4,500 years before present.Sidwell, Paul. 2021. The Red River is the second largest river in Vietnam and one of the five largest rivers on the East Asia coast. Its catchment covers parts of China and Vietnam and its water and sediment discharges greatly influence the hydrology in the Gulf of Tonkin. ==Delta economy== In 2003, of the 78 million people in Vietnam, almost a third (24 million) live in the Red River basin, including over 17 million people in the delta itself. There are many large industrial zones in the Red River Delta clustering in [[Viet Tri]], Hanoi, Haiphong and [[Nam Dinh]]. Most of the population works in rice cultivation but the delta region hosts other important economic activities such as [[fisheries]], [[aquaculture]], [[land reclamation]] for agriculture, harbor construction, [[mangrove]] [[forestry]], etc. The socio-economic development in the delta is also affected by seasonal [[typhoon|storms]], [[flooding]], [[coastal erosion]], [[silting]], [[salt water intrusion]], etc. Though the Red River Delta makes up only 5% of Vietnam's land, 30% of the country's population live there, making it the most densely populated part of the country. 80% of the population are employed in agriculture, but the agricultural lands of the delta amount to only about .3-.5 [[hectare]]s per household, making the limited supply of arable lands a significant constraint to improving living standards. Agriculturally the Red River Delta is the second most important [[rice cultivation|rice-producing]] area in Vietnam, accounting for 20% of the national crop. Production of rice is close to optimal with very little [[yield gap]] to exploit and employing [[double cropping]] techniques to achieve close to maximum yields. However the rich soil of the delta does present a possibility of crop diversification and there is potential for further development of aquaculture.Edwards et al (eds.) ''Rural Aquaculture'', CABI publishing, page 56. With these developmental pressures the estuarine environment and ecosystem face degradation due to threats of pollution, over-fishing and aquaculture destroying natural habitats.{{cite journal|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258993253|title=Researches in estuarine environment and ecosystem of Red River: An overview on activities and results|first=Tran|last=Thanh|date=1 January 2003|journal=MarINE Environment and Resources. The Red River Delta or Hong River Delta (Vietnamese: Đồng bằng sông Hồng) is the flat low-lying plain formed by the Red River and its distributaries merging with the Thái Bình River in Northern Vietnam. Hồng (紅) is a Sino-Vietnamese word for "red" or "crimson". The delta has the smallest area but highest population and population density of all regions in Vietnam. The region, measuring some 15,000 square kilometres (6,000 sq mi) is well protected by a network of dikes. It is an agriculturally rich and densely populated area. Most of the land is devoted to rice cultivation.
The Red River Delta, after the 2025 merger of Vietnamese provinces and cities, includes four provinces, together with two municipalities (the capital Hanoi, and the port of Haiphong). It had a population of almost 23 million in 2019.
In 2021, Paul Sidwell proposed that the locus of Proto-Austroasiatic languages was in this area about 4,000–4,500 years before present. The Hong River Delta is the cradle of the Vietnamese nation. Water puppetry originated in the rice paddies here. The region was bombed by United States warplanes during the Vietnam War. The region was designated as the Red River Delta Biosphere Reserve as part of UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme in 2004.
